column1: # *** PABLO ARMANDO LERENA AND MARY SEPTIMA TAYLOR - PAPERS SUPPLIED BY DAVID, 13 OCTOBER 2026 ***
# Eight items. Four are published as images (the 1916 marriage extract, the church register page, Roque's 1936 marriage, and the
# colourised crop); the Northam death entry, the 1925 passenger list and the 2026 photographs are described and not shown.
# Several other files in the folder were duplicates of documents this archive already holds (the 1950 death notice, the 1973 death notice
# of Roque, the Exeter prize list, the Roque baptism annotations) and are not repeated here.

column4: what it adds, and what it does not

column2: St Dominic's, Wynberg: printed 'Extract from the Register of Marriages', certified 7 April 1916 (signature read as C. McCarthy)
column3: Pablo Armando Lerena and Mary Septima Taylor married according to the Rites of the Roman Catholic Church on the 3rd September 1905 by Rev. B. W. Glynn; witnesses J. B. Worthington and H. Lautenbach; offering 2s 6d to Nazareth House.
column4: *** THE EXTRACT SAYS 1905; THE REGISTER SAYS 1911. *** The day, month, priest and both witnesses match the Duplicate Original Register (3 September 1911, entry 160, Glynn; Worthington and Lautenbach), so it is the same marriage with the year changed. 1911 stands: the register gives their ages as 29 and 27, which fit births in 1882 and 1884 and not 23 and 21; Roque was baptised in June 1911 'three months before' it. A 1905 marriage would make Roque, born 25 November 1905, a child of the marriage; a 1911 one makes him five years older than it. WHETHER THE YEAR IS A CLERK'S SLIP OR WAS CHOSEN IS NOT SHOWN, and no reason for asking for an extract in 1916 is known. It is the only document that says 1905.

column2: Photograph of a marriage-register page: the couple's signature lines, with the residence column
column3: 'Pablo Armando Lerena' and 'Mary Septima Taylor' written one above the other; against them, in the residence column, 'Ebenezer Road, Wynberg'.
column4: A different address from the civil duplicate, which gives Diep River for both. The page is not identified in the photograph (the book and year are not shown), so it is NOT yet tied to a named register. Two readings: they gave one address to the priest and another to the civil register, or one is a postal district. Ebenezer Road, Wynberg is a street, so it can be looked for in the 1911 street directory.

column2: Duplicate Original Marriage Register, no. 14/1936: Catholic Church, Mayfair, Johannesburg, 21 September 1936
column3: Luis Roque Armando Lerena, 29 (overwritten 30), born Cape Province, bachelor, STEWARD, of 6a Bartlett Road, Mayfair West; Rosaline Wilhelmina Chappell born Forbes, 33, born Cape Province, widow, of the same address; married after banns, without ante-nuptial contract, 'Certificate of Master of Supreme Court enclosed'; witnesses A. W. Webber and S. Brophy; the priest signs as McCarthy.
column4: The church's marginal note on Roque's baptism says 21 September 1936 at St Joseph's (Rev. P. McCarthy, O.M.I.); this is the civil entry for the same marriage and the church is the Mayfair one. NEW: his trade, steward, and a Mayfair address in 1936. The bride is a WIDOW, which is why Chappell is her married name and Forbes her maiden name, as the register already says. The age on the page is corrected in the register's own hand, so 29 or 30 is not settled; 25 November 1905 would make him 30.

column2: Death entry, Bideford registration district, Northam sub-district, 1900, no. 83 (a copy; not published)
column3: Mary Ann Hellen Taylor, female, 56, wife of William Taylor, Army Pensioner, died 21 April 1900 at Sweet Home Terrace, Northam; chronic nephritis, dropsy, valvular heart disease, bronchitis, certified by Allan Mahood(?); informant Mary Septima Taylor, daughter, 'present at the death'; registered 23 April 1900 by William Ashplant.
column4: The date, the address and the cause of her mother's death, and that SHE WAS THERE: Mary Septima, sixteen, signs as informant. It agrees with what the archive already held (mother died in 1900, father in November 1902) and adds the street. The doctor's name is not certain. Not published: a General Register Office entry, transcribed.

column2: UK incoming passenger list, 'Arundel Castle' (Union-Castle Mail S.S. Co.), arrived Southampton 14 December 1925 from South Africa (Natal) via Cape Town, 1st class, line 67 (not published)
column3: 'Taylor, Mary S.', wife, 42; proposed address 'Ladies' Carlton Club, Chesterfield Gardens, Mayfair, London'; last permanent residence entered as a ditto mark; intended residence England.
column4: *** A CANDIDATE, AND A WEAK ONE. *** For: the initials, 'Mary S.', the age within a year (she was 41 on that date by her register birth of 17 September 1884, and the form says 42), the port and the Cape Town embarkation. Against: she is entered under her MAIDEN name when she had been Mrs Lerena for fourteen years, as 'wife' of nobody named on the list; she would be leaving a fourteen-month-old Nuno; and a London ladies' club is an unexpected address for her, though nothing here rules it out. It may be a different Mary S. Taylor. TEST: whether a Lerena or a Taylor of that age sails back in 1926, and whether the 1920s Cape Town papers note a Mrs Lerena going to England. The piece reference is not on the image. Not published, because it is a National Archives record: cited and transcribed, not republished.

column2: A close-up of the small girl in the Taylor group photograph, colourised by David
column3: A girl of five or six, seated between the knees of a man, in a dark dress and laced boots.
column4: The group photograph is already on this page; this is a crop of the figure David identifies as Mary Septima, in colour. THE COLOURS ARE THE COLOURISING SOFTWARE'S, NOT THE PHOTOGRAPH'S, and say nothing about the dress. The identification is David's, from the family, and is the same one the group photograph's own entry makes.

column2: Two photographs taken in 2026: the house at 7 Forth Road, and the grave at Maitland (not published)
column3: Captions added by the photographer: 'Pablo Armando Lerena's house, 7 Forth Rd, Wynberg - 1950'; 'Lerena's grave, plot 7719G - Maitland, Cape Town, 1950 - Pablo Armando, 1935 - Mary Septima, 1947 - Careen Marie'.
column4: Two disagreements to settle, neither important: the house is captioned WYNBERG where the 1950 death notice says NEWLANDS (adjoining suburbs; the notice gives No. 7 Forth Road, Newlands), and the plot is captioned 7719G where the interment register has 7719 and 7719A. The caption's 'G' may be the cemetery office's own lettering for the same grave. NOT PUBLISHED, because living people stand in both pictures. A house and a grave with nobody in front of them would be welcome.
